correctness.rationale: For p=4k+3, plane Hasse-Witt expansion of F=Y⁴−XZ(X−Z)(X−tZ) has Y exponent multiple of four only in the middle diagonal Cech coefficient, yielding diag(0,-H_m(t),0), m=(p−1)/2, H_m=Σbinom(m,j)²t^j. Stable p-rank is 1 or 0; a-number is 2 or 3. The p-prime double-cover splitting identifies an everywhere-superspecial Prym; the Legendre elliptic quotient is supersingular at precisely H_m=0. Its hypergeometric ODE and nonzero endpoint values imply degree-m polynomial has exactly m distinct smooth roots. This is an all-prime algebraic proof; finite script claims are corroboration only.
